name: Extended superior scapular approach for periprosthetic spine fractures
aliases: scapular-spine approach around a shoulder prosthesis
corridor: Incision along the palpable scapular spine, sharp division of deltoid from the spine and acromial base leaving a cuff for reattachment

positioning.text: Position according to the fracture; extra-articular scapular-spine fractures are generally approached from posterior so the spine and acromial base can be palpated.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the scapular spine, which is usually easy to palpate, and the acromial base.

incision.text: Incise along the scapular spine; length depends on the exposure required.

superficial_interval.text: Sharply divide deltoid from its insertion on the scapular spine and the acromial base, leaving a small tissue border so the muscle can be repaired.

deep_interval.text: Work on the extra-articular spine. This is not a full Judet elevation of the scapular body and is not a saber-cut over the AC joint, though a saber cut can be joined if the acromion also needs exposure.

layers.text: Skin, deltoid origin on the spine and acromion, then the extra-articular scapular spine.

structures_at_risk.text: The deltoid origin is at risk if no cuff is left for reattachment. A full posterior body dissection would add the suprascapular nerve at the spinoglenoid notch, which this limited spine window does not require.

danger_zones.text: Detaching deltoid flush with bone without a repair cuff prevents secure reattachment to the remaining deltoid cuff on the acromion and spine.

retraction_hazards.text: Release only as much deltoid as the spine fracture requires so the muscle can be repaired to the leftover cuff.

exposure.text: Shows extra-articular oblique or transverse spine fractures around reverse or anatomic prostheses; these fractures are more often seen with reverse arthroplasty.

limitations.text: Does not expose the scapular body or glenoid the way a Judet approach does, and does not replace a saber-cut AC window.

indications.text: Used for extra-articular oblique or transverse scapular-spine fractures around reverse or anatomic prostheses.

closure.text: Reattach the deltoid base and its deep and superficial fascia to the remaining deltoid cuff on the acromion and spine, then close subcutaneous fascia and skin.

complications.text: Failure to leave a repair cuff or to reattach deltoid leaves a detached origin on the spine and acromion.

procedure_applications.condition: An oblique or transverse scapular-spine fracture around a reverse or anatomic prosthesis is plated from the spine

questions.question: Where is the incision for the extended superior scapular approach?
questions.answer: Along the palpable scapular spine, with length set by the needed exposure.

questions.question: How is deltoid taken off the spine so it can be repaired?
questions.answer: Divide it from the spine and acromial base while leaving a small tissue border, then reattach that cuff to the remaining deltoid on the acromion and spine.

questions.question: Which prosthesis is more often associated with this spine fracture pattern?
